reviewers.agent: general-purpose subagent, separate context; sole arbiter (round 1 formally; rounds 2-4 verified in-line against the tree)

records.finding: The verify block presented `go install .../cmd/shortfall@latest` as 'the check that counts', but go install pkg@version refuses any module whose go.mod carries replace directives; cmd/shortfall carries three.
records.evidence: `go help install`: "it must not contain directives (replace and exclude) that would cause it to be interpreted differently than if it were the main module"; cmd/shortfall/go.mod carries three replaces. Reproduced against a file:// proxy.
records.reason: Confirmed against `go help install` and reproduced by the cross-examiner against a file:// proxy. The command was removed, the reason documented, and the underlying decision filed as workspace-47f rather than taken here.

records.finding: Step 5's close named exactly two preconditions for go install ('Both are needed') when a third — the replace directives — makes it impossible regardless.
records.evidence: docs/quickstart.md: "Once the repository is public **and** the release tags are pushed ... Both are needed" - contradicted by cmd/shortfall/go.mod's replace lines.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: The file header said 'there is no fork story here' while the same diff added a fork-PR credential guard to that file.
records.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:8 "there is no fork story here" vs the fork guard added at ci.yml:307 in the same diff.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: The pin-loop comment said 'six reassuring bootstrap lines' after the loop grew to seven paths; the count is the comment's whole argument for the rev-parse guard.
records.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:268 "six reassuring bootstrap lines" vs a seven-path loop at :272.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: .warden/checkers was added to the pin list but exists nowhere, so the else branch printed a bootstrap line every run, normalising the tell of a broken pin.
records.evidence: `ls .warden/checkers` -> No such file or directory; `git cat-file -e main:.warden/checkers` -> exit 128.
records.reason: Fixed twice. First by silencing the absent-from-both case; then, after round 2 showed the entry also invalidated the loop's add-only safety argument, the entry was removed entirely and the reasoning recorded in the comment.

records.finding: The fork guard was copied verbatim into the corpus job, which is push-to-main only, so both its comment and its operator-facing message were false there.
records.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:349 `if: github.event_name == 'push'` and :19-20 `push: branches: [main]`, vs the fork-worded message inside the corpus job.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: 'Each nested go.mod carries replace ... => ../../..' was wrong for cmd/shortfall and the test modules, which are one level shallower.
records.evidence: cmd/shortfall/go.mod uses `=> ../..`; only adapters/<kind>/<name>/ are three levels down.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: The branch-relay command block — the entire new outside-contribution path — did not work: `git push origin FETCH_HEAD:contrib/<name>` is rejected because the destination is unqualified.
records.evidence: Executed literally in a scratch repo: "error: The destination you provided is not a full refname ... hint: Did you mean 'FETCH_HEAD:refs/heads/contrib/someone-topic'?" exit=1.
records.reason: Reproduced failing in a scratch repo, then fixed to FETCH_HEAD:refs/heads/... with a note on why the namespace cannot be inferred.

records.finding: A cross-reference added by the round-1 fix pointed at 'the end of step 5'; the explanation is under ## Next.
records.evidence: docs/quickstart.md headings: 197 `## 5. What you get`, 227 `## Next`; the go-install paragraph begins at 239, inside Next.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: 'The check that counts' was stated unconditionally although neither go get line can run while the module is private, contradicting README and quickstart; and go get resolves published tags, never the working tree, so it cannot verify this diff's bumps.
records.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md "The check that counts" vs docs/quickstart.md:14 and README.md:73, both stating go get cannot resolve a private module.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: The block ended on `go build ./...` in a scratch module with no .go files: it matches no packages and exits 0, reading as a compile check while compiling nothing.
records.evidence: `go mod init scratch` then `go build ./...` in an empty module: "go: warning: ./... matched no packages", exit 0.
records.reason: Replaced with a heredoc main.go importing biz and the prometheus adapter, then go mod tidy + go build. The snippet was compiled and run against the local tree (prints 'USD 0.01').

records.finding: The fix replaced one never-published version with another: every first-party require now names v0.2.0, which is not tagged either, and the correspondence to the release tag was unwritten and unenforced.
records.evidence: `git tag -l` -> v0.1.0 only; every nested go.mod now requires v0.2.0, which is not tagged.
records.reason: Addressed by test/modgraph plus the documented tag fan-out. The residue is stated plainly: modgraph reads the tree, never the proxy, so it cannot confirm publication.

records.finding: A bug whose defining property was 'nothing went red' shipped with prose and no mechanical guard, so it could re-land silently.
records.evidence: scripts/ci-go.sh:144 enumerates go.mod files but never inspects them; no test in the tree read go.mod contents before this diff.
records.reason: Added test/modgraph, following the repo's existing checker-module pattern. Watched failing on both real cases (v0.0.0 placeholder, version skew) before being trusted.

records.finding: Adding .warden/checkers to the pin loop invalidated the stated add-only safety argument: git checkout -- path deletes nothing, so a PR ADDING a checker keeps it and the gate would execute it with the deploy key on disk.
records.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:257-261 "git checkout <ref> -- path ... deletes nothing ... Nothing invokes a script by an unknown name" vs adding an executable directory to the loop at :272.
records.reason: Entry removed. Pinning an executable directory needs remove-then-restore, which changes the pin's semantics and is its own reviewed change; the reasoning is now in the loop's comment.

records.finding: The comment claimed the entry guaranteed pinning 'the day one lands', which is exactly the day the path is absent from base and runs unpinned.
records.evidence: ci.yml comment "the day one lands it must already be pinned" adjacent to the elif branch that runs the PR's own copy on exactly that day.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: The rewritten header grouped corpus ingest with warden gate as fork-blocked and asserted 'No job here is skipped on a fork', but corpus is push-only and skipped on every PR.
records.evidence: ci.yml:7-14 "No job here is skipped on a fork" vs :360 `if: github.event_name == 'push'`.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: The round-1 fix traded one wrong statement for another: four of the seven test/ modules neither require nor replace the core module.
records.evidence: test/blankline/go.mod, test/licensehdr/go.mod, test/symbolcheck/go.mod, test/wikisync/go.mod carry no first-party require or replace.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: The PR rewrote the CLI-acquisition story in quickstart and CONTRIBUTING but left README's Install and Report sections describing the old one, giving no way to obtain the CLI it demonstrates.
records.evidence: README.md:69-76 (Install) and README.md:141-145 (`shortfall impact ...`) vs docs/quickstart.md:239-246 after this diff.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: Two of the three repo-level tests were loop-and-assert bodies that could execute zero times and still PASS; only one carried a guard, and loadMods' guard was on file count, not on edges understood.
records.evidence: Reviewer pointed repoRoot at a two-module fixture with no first-party requires: TestNoFirstPartyRequireNamesAPlaceholderVersion and TestEveryFirstPartyRequireHasALocalReplace both PASSED having inspected nothing.
records.reason: Reproduced by the reviewer against a fixture. Fixed with a shared guard in loadMods: zero unparsed first-party lines, and a first-party require floor recorded against the real count.

records.finding: ParseMod had no failure channel: any go.mod shape it did not recognise contributed silently nothing, so a whole file could drop out of all three checks with the suite green. The reviewer reproduced the ORIGINAL bug sitting green behind a quoted module path.
records.evidence: Reviewer fixture with sub/go.mod carrying `require "<prefix>/adapters/query/sql" v0.0.0` (quoted, no replace): all three tests PASS, subtests emitted only for the other module.
records.reason: Added the Unparsed channel — a first-party line the parser cannot read now fails the run — plus quoted-path handling. This was the most valuable finding of the review.

records.finding: The paragraph still described 'both go get lines' after the snippet below it had been rewritten to go mod tidy / go build.
records.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:207 "both go get lines fail on that alone" vs the fenced block at 210-224, whose commands are go mod init / cat > main.go / go mod tidy / go build.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: The replace-depth paragraph missed that loggolden and promgolden also carry sibling-adapter replaces, and omitted test/modgraph from the standalone-checker list this PR adds.
records.evidence: test/loggolden/go.mod replaces cloudwatch and cwinsights; test/promgolden/go.mod replaces promql; test/modgraph/go.mod is a fifth standalone checker.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: The table checked Requires by exact length but Replaces only for presence, so a parser marking everything replaced passed the whole table.
records.evidence: modgraph_test.go replaces loop `for _, path := range c.replaces` runs zero times for five of seven cases, and no case asserted len(got.Replaces).
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: The Replaces godoc and the test name both asserted a LOCAL replacement while the parser never inspected the target.
records.evidence: ParseMod on `replace <prefix> => example.com/fork v1.2.3` yielded replaces[<prefix>]=true with no inspection of the target.
records.reason: Added IsLocalTarget with its own table test, and the check now rejects a module-path target.

records.finding: A replace with a version on the left — what `go mod edit -replace=path@version=target` writes — was unrecognised in both forms, producing a false accusation.
records.evidence: ParseMod on `replace <prefix> v0.2.0 => ../..` yielded requires={<prefix>:v0.2.0} replaces={} - a false 'does not replace it' accusation.
records.reason: Rewritten to locate the arrow by index rather than fixed position; covered by a table case.

records.finding: The skew failure message claimed adopters would fail, which is untrue — minimal version selection picks the highest and resolves.
records.evidence: modgraph_test.go message "fails only for an adopter"; MVS resolves differing requires to the highest with no error.
records.reason: Message rewritten to describe the real consequence: silent drift until a release tags one version and the stragglers name another.

records.finding: The replace requirement was enforced unconditionally while its own message framed it as conditional; after publication, dropping a replace becomes correct rather than a defect.
records.evidence: modgraph_test.go asserted m.Replaces[path] for every first-party require with no condition, while CONTRIBUTING names dropping cmd/shortfall's replaces as the tracked path to a working go install.
records.reason: Renamed and given a doc comment naming it a deliberate pre-publication ratchet, to be revisited by the change that drops the replaces.

records.finding: %w on an *exec.ExitError renders only 'exit status 128', discarding git's captured reason, in the one place the checker can fail for infrastructure reasons.
records.evidence: TrackedModFiles("/") -> "git ls-files: exit status 128" with git's "fatal: not a git repository" discarded by %w on an ExitError.
records.reason: Surfaces ExitError.Stderr, with a table test watched failing when the branch is defeated.

records.finding: The docstring claimed the go toolchain is silent about 'exactly the pair' of conditions when the package's own third invariant is a third such condition, invisible to go because of go.work's use list rather than because of a replace.
records.evidence: Deleting the replace from adapters/query/promql/go.mod: go build/vet/test in that module all exit 0, while test/modgraph goes red - a third go-silent condition where the docstring said 'exactly the pair'.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: The new ExitError.Stderr branch had no test in either direction, and TrackedModFiles was the only exported function with no direct test.
records.evidence: grep for TrackedModFiles in modgraph_test.go found it only inside loadMods on the success path; the ExitError branch had no test.
records.reason: Added TestTrackedModFilesExplainsAGitFailure, table-driven over a non-git dir and a missing dir; watched failing when the Stderr surfacing is removed.

records.finding: The docstring credited the non-local-replace guard to this checker, but go.work makes that a hard conflict go refuses first — the same trap the surrounding paragraph warns about.
records.evidence: Setting a module-path replace produced `go: conflicting replacements ... EXIT=1` before any test ran - go's failure, credited to this checker.
records.reason: Reworded to say the guard is belt to go's braces and why it stays.

records.finding: The Replaces comment said targets are kept 'verbatim' while a trailing version on the right-hand side is dropped, and the table case name implied the opposite.
records.evidence: ParseMod on `replace <prefix> => example.com/f v1.2.3` yields target `example.com/f`; the version is dropped though the comment says 'verbatim'.
records.reason: Fixed in this branch; see the commit body.

records.finding: Go 1.24's `tool (` block was swallowed by the single-line catch-all, so a first-party tool path inside it became an unreadable line and failed the run — a false failure on a legitimate go.mod, and inconsistent with the single-line form.
records.evidence: ParseMod on a `tool (` block containing a first-party path yielded unparsed=[<prefix>/cmd/shortfall]; the single-line `tool` form yielded unparsed=[].
records.reason: tool( and godebug( now open ignored blocks; a table case pins both forms agreeing.

records.finding: The floor's comment described a margin against a number it never recorded, making the margin unverifiable and silently erodible.
records.evidence: Instrumented count over the tracked set: 24 files, 23 first-party requires; the comment recorded neither, so the stated margin was unverifiable.
records.reason: The comment now records 23 requires across 24 files, states the margin's purpose, and notes the calibration that matters: 12 arrive via the block form and 11 via the single-line form, so losing either trips the floor.
